26 In a double-slit interference experiment, light of frequency 6.0 × 1014
Hz is incident on a pair of
slits. Bright fringes that are 3.0 mm apart are observed on a screen some distance away.
What is the separation of the bright fringes when the frequency of the light is changed to
5.0 × 1014
Hz?
A
1.8 mm
B
2.5 mm
C
3.0 mm
D
3.6 mm

hints: Notice the fringe spacing is $3.0 \text{ mm}$ for $6.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ and only the frequency changes to $5.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ - the slit separation and screen distance stay fixed.
Connect fringe spacing to wavelength with $w = \lambda D/a$, and wavelength to frequency with $c = f\lambda$, so $w$ is proportional to $1/f$.
Compare the two cases by ratio: new spacing $= 3.0 \text{ mm} \times (6.0 \times 10^{14})/(5.0 \times 10^{14})$ - check whether it should be larger or smaller than $3.0 \text{ mm}$.
walkthrough: Identify the fixed quantities: slit separation $a$ and screen distance $D$ are unchanged, while frequency $f$ changes from $6.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ to $5.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$.
State the governing rules: fringe spacing is $w = \lambda D/a$ and wave speed is $c = f\lambda$, so $\lambda = c/f$.
Combine them to show $w = cD/(af)$, so for fixed $c$, $D$ and $a$, the spacing $w$ is inversely proportional to $f$.
Set up the ratio: $w_2/w_1 = f_1/f_2$ because $cD/a$ cancels.
Substitute values with units: $w_2 = 3.0 \text{ mm} \times (6.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz})/(5.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}) = 3.0 \text{ mm} \times 6.0/5.0$.
Calculate the intermediate result: $6.0/5.0 = 1.2$, so $w_2 = 3.0 \text{ mm} \times 1.2 = 3.6 \text{ mm}$. Lower frequency gives longer wavelength and wider fringes. This is option D.

A.explanation: Too small. It assumes the fringe spacing decreases when frequency decreases, which reverses the $\lambda$ dependence.

B.explanation: It gives $3.0 \times 5.0/6.0 = 2.5 \text{ mm}$, assuming fringe spacing is directly proportional to frequency instead of inversely proportional.

C.explanation: It assumes changing frequency from $6.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ to $5.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ does not change wavelength and fringe spacing.

D.explanation: Lower frequency means larger wavelength, so fringe spacing increases by factor $6.0/5.0$ to $3.6 \text{ mm}$.
